You see only the question and its options. You do not see the answer key, the stored solution, or any student comment. Do not guess what the expected answer is. Work it out.

Rules:

- If your result matches none of the options, set "status" to "no_option_matches" and give your result in "value".
- A blank or missing option never matches. Do not guess what it was meant to say.
- If more than one option is correct in a single-correct question, or none is, say so in "note".
- Answer format:
  - single-correct: one letter, for example "B"
  - multiple-correct: every correct letter, comma separated, for example "A, C, D"

request.user:
Subject: Physics
Question type: integer answer (no options)

A body of mass 2 kg is kept by pressing to a vertical wall by a force of 100 N. The friction between wall and body is 0.3. Then the frictional force is equal to

result.working:
Pressing force 100 N is horizontal, so normal reaction N = 100 N.
Maximum (limiting) friction = μN = 0.3 × 100 = 30 N.
Weight of body = mg = 2 × 10 = 20 N (g = 10 m/s²).
Weight 20 N < limiting friction 30 N, so the body stays at rest (static).
Static friction balances the weight: f = mg = 20 N.
result.note: Assumes g = 10 m/s². The force of 100 N is taken to be horizontal (pressing the body against the wall). The frictional force is static friction, not μN = 30 N. With g = 9.8 m/s² it would be 19.6 N.
